name: GA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district fundamentals with a large partisan lean favoring the incumbent party
Lucy McBath's incumbency and large financial advantage over a barely funded challenger
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent
No public polling or expert ratings available, leaving some uncertainty
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to McBath: the district's partisan lean, her incumbency, and a fundraising gap of roughly ninety to one against Kevin Martin all favor the Democrat, and markets agree at about 96 percent. With no polls or expert ratings to refine the picture, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-driven margin of a high-twenties Democratic win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race, or significant outside spending against McBath, would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lucy McBath, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a district whose underlying partisanship strongly favors her party. She enters the general election with a large cash advantage, roughly $676,000 on hand, while Republican Kevin Martin has raised about $10,000 and reported only $100 in reserve, with no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets put her chances near 96 percent.

The main limitation is the absence of public polling and expert ratings for this race, so the forecast leans on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Those all point the same way: a comfortable Democratic win, likely by a margin in the mid-to-high twenties, with McBath a heavy favorite.
